cards.text: Here's a vision, friend. It came to Isaiah son of Amoz, a prophet, while four kings of Judah reigned: Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah. FOUR kings! I couldn't even outlast ONE shiny new cookie stamper.

cards.question: Isaiah's vision is about two places. Which two?

cards.text: Then Isaiah calls out, "Listen, O heavens, and give ear, O earth," because the LORD has spoken. When you call the sky AND the ground to listen, nobody gets to be on mute.

cards.question: The LORD says, "I have raised children and brought them up." What did those children do?

answers.text: They asked Him for a king

cards.text: Then the LORD points to the barn. The ox knows its owner, and the donkey knows its master's manger.

cards.question: True or false: The LORD says His people know Him the way the ox knows its owner.

cards.text: So the DONKEY is out here knowing more than the people. Then Isaiah cries out, "Alas, O sinful nation, a people laden with iniquity."

cards.question: Isaiah says the people have forsaken the LORD and despised the Holy One of Israel. What else have they done?

answers.text: Sold the treasures of His temple
Built a new altar in Egypt

cards.text: Isaiah asks them, "Why do you want more beatings? Why do you keep rebelling?" That's hitting snooze NINE times and acting shocked you're late.

cards.question: Isaiah talks to the nation like it's one hurt body. True or false: he says only the head is hurt and the rest of the body is sound.
From the sole of the foot to the top of the head, Isaiah sees wounds and welts and festering sores. What's been done for them?

answers.text: No one has cleansed or bandaged them
They've been bandaged with great care
They've been soothed with oil each day

cards.text: Now Isaiah talks about the land itself. It's desolate, and the cities are burned with fire.

cards.question: Isaiah says ___ are devouring Judah's fields right in front of them.

cards.text: Isaiah pictures the Daughter of Zion like a shelter in a vineyard, like a shack in a cucumber field, like a city besieged. Ain't NOBODY ever said, "Meet me at the cucumber shack."

cards.question: Isaiah compares the Daughter of Zion to a shack out in a field. What's the picture?

cards.text: Then Isaiah says "us," so he's in this too. He brings up Sodom and Gomorrah, the cities the LORD rained sulfur and fire on (Genesis 19:24).

cards.question: Judah hasn't become like Sodom and Gomorrah only because the LORD of Hosts left them a few ___.

cards.text: Isaiah just said they ALMOST ended up like Sodom and Gomorrah. Now he calls them to hear the word of the LORD, and friend, wait till you hear how he says hello.

cards.question: Isaiah calls his listeners to hear the word of the LORD. What does he call their rulers?

cards.text: Then the LORD speaks: "What good to Me is your multitude of sacrifices?" He says He's full from their burnt offerings of rams and the fat of well-fed cattle.

cards.question: True or false: The LORD says He delights in the blood of bulls and lambs and goats.

cards.text: When they come before Him, the LORD asks who required all this trampling of His courts. TRAMPLING, friend, like a Black Friday crowd hitting the doors at five in the morning.

cards.question: The LORD tells the people to stop bringing Him something. What is it?

cards.text: He says their incense is detestable to Him. He hates their New Moons and appointed feasts, and He's weary of bearing them.

cards.question: True or false: The LORD says what He cannot endure is iniquity in a solemn assembly.

cards.text: When they spread out their hands in prayer, the LORD says He will hide His eyes from them. Even if they multiply their prayers, He will not listen.

cards.question: The LORD won't listen to all those prayers. He says their hands are covered with ___.
Then the LORD says, "Wash and cleanse yourselves." What does He tell them to remove from His sight?

cards.text: The LORD says, "Stop doing evil!" and "Learn to do right; seek justice and correct the oppressor." So it's not enough to stop hitting snooze, friend. You gotta actually get UP.

cards.question: The LORD tells them to seek justice and correct the oppressor. Who does He tell them to stand up for?

cards.text: "Come now, let us reason together," says the LORD. Their sins are like scarlet, as red as crimson.

cards.question: True or false: The LORD says sins like scarlet can never be made white.

cards.text: White as SNOW! Like WOOL! Then the LORD lays out two roads: one for the willing and obedient, and one for those who resist and rebel.

cards.question: The LORD says the willing and obedient will eat the ___ of the land, and those who resist and rebel will be devoured by the ___.

cards.text: And it closes with this: "For the mouth of the LORD has spoken." When He says it, friend, that's not a maybe. That's a sealed box.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 4 quotes "I have raised children and brought them up.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 7 quotes "Alas, O sinful nation, a people laden with iniquity.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The opening card has 4 sentences: "Here's a vision, friend." / "It came to Isaiah son of Amoz..." / "FOUR kings!" / "I couldn't even outlast ONE shiny new cookie stamper."

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: Isaiah is introduced as "a prophet." That fact comes from outside Isaiah 1:1-20, and the card gives no reference for it (for example, Isaiah 37:2).

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The joke "Ain't NOBODY ever said, 'Meet me at the cucumber shack'" says that no one goes to the shack. That gives away the answer to card 15, "Abandoned and alone," and rules out "Crowded with guests."

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The card restates Isaiah 1:9 ("Isaiah just said they ALMOST ended up like Sodom and Gomorrah") but cites only Isaiah 1:10.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The story card has 3 sentences: the LORD's quotes, "So it's not enough to stop hitting snooze, friend." and "You gotta actually get UP."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: "Their sins are like scarlet, as red as crimson" drops the "though" from Isaiah 1:18 ("Though your sins are like scarlet... though they are as red as crimson"). This turns the LORD's conditional wording into a flat statement.
The story card has 3 sentences: "White as SNOW!" / "Like WOOL!" / "Then the LORD lays out two roads..."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The story card has 3 sentences: "And it closes with this: ..." / "When He says it, friend, that's not a maybe." / "That's a sealed box."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
